paper_metadata.title: Evaluation of cyclic hot corrosion behaviour of detonation gun sprayed Cr3C2–25%NiCr coatings on nickel- and iron-based superalloys

evidence.quote: Cr 3C2–NiCr cermet coatings were deposited on two Ni-based superalloys, namely superni 75, superni 718 and one Fe-based superalloy superfer 800H by detonation-gun thermal spray process.

Detonation-gun (Model: Awaaz) process was used to apply coatings on all six surfaces (sides) of the superalloys at SVX Powder M Surface Engineering Pvt. Ltd, New Delhi (India).

The spraying parameters were, oxygen/acetylene ﬂow rate (ratio) — 1:1.21, carrier gas ﬂow rate (N 2) — 1.2 (m3/h), frequency 3 shots/s, spot size diameter 20 mm, spraying distance from nozzle 165 mm and powder ﬂow rate 1.0 to 2.0 g per shot.

The formation of spinel of NiCr 2O4 via solid phase reaction between NiO and Cr 2O3 in the oxide scales has been reported by Xin Ren et al. [27], which also helps to develop oxidation resistance as the spinel phase that usually has lower diffusion coefﬁcients of the cations and anions than those in their parent oxides [28].

Chromia is the best oxide to resist hot corrosion in molten sulfates, as it preferentially reacts with O 2− in molten sulfates to form chromate. The chromate will stabilize the melt chemistry, and consequently prevent the dissolution of the protective oxide scale [26].
